'''Robert Horton Romer''' (April 15, 1931 – November 2, 2025) was an American [[physicist]].

== Life and career ==
Romer was born in [[Chicago, Illinois]], the son of Alfred Sherwood Romer and Ruth Hibbard. He was raised in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]], and attended [[Amherst College]], earning his [[Bachelor of Arts|BA degree]] in 1952. He also attended [[Princeton University]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[physics]] in 1955.<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.romerfamily.com/Robert-H-Romer-Obituary|title=Robert H. Romer|work=Romer Family|access-date=June 5, 2026}}</ref>

Romer served as a professor in the department of physics at Amherst College from 1955 to 2001. During his years as a professor, from 1988 to 2001, he served as [[Editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[American Journal of Physics]]'',<ref name="a" /><ref name="b">{{Cite web|url=https://www.amherst.edu/news/memoriam/node/935333|title=Robert H. Romer '52 (1931–2025)|work=[[Amherst College]]|access-date=June 5, 2026}}</ref> and in 1991, he was named a [[List of fellows of the American Physical Society|fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]], "for his innovative energy-based physics textbook and other writings on the energy problem, and for his editorial work for the entire physics community".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship?q=robert%20romer&af=true|title=APS Fellow Archive|work=[[American Physical Society]]|access-date=June 5, 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
Romer was married twice. In 1953, he married Diana Hayes. Their marriage lasted until her death in 1992. After the death of his first wife, he then married Betty Steele in 1994. His second marriage lasted until his death in 2025.<ref name="a" />

Romer died at his home in [[Amherst, Massachusetts]] on November 2, 2025, at the age of 94.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/gazettenet/name/robert-romer-obituary?id=60000050|title=Robert Romer Obituary (1931-2025)|work=[[Daily Hampshire Gazette]]|date=November 11, 2025|access-date=June 5, 2026|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref>
